# ADR-0068: Declare serve devices as the placement authority

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-10-23

**References:** [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md), [RFC-0006](../rfc/RFC-0006.md), [RFC-0005](../rfc/RFC-0005.md)

## Context

[RFC-0003:C-SERVE-PARALLELISM](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-parallelism) gives servers nine framework-neutral parallelism components and leaves their algebra to each integration, which derives the whole-replica device count that placement consumes. Integrations read the same declaration differently. SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and TokenSpeed treat `outer.tensor_parallel_size` as the replica world that attention data parallelism divides, so `outer.tensor_parallel_size = 8` with `attention.data_parallel_size = 8` places 8 devices. vLLM treats it as per-data-parallel-rank tensor parallelism that data parallelism multiplies, so the same declaration places 64. Because the clause leaves the algebra to integrations, each reading is that integration's own choice; no neutral rule picks one. [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-CONTEXT-PARALLELISM](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-context-parallelism) adds a role-dependent exception that lets a prefill role's context parallelism multiply devices.

Framework layouts keep getting finer and more per-component: prefill and decode context parallelism are different mechanisms, attention and experts take different data-parallel and expert-parallel splits, and engines such as a data-parallel × expert-parallel Specialized Engine combine them in one process. A neutral vocabulary would have to track all of that to stay meaningful.

The control plane itself uses the shape for two facts only: the whole-replica device count for placement, and the attention data-parallel rank count that priming fan-out and the built-in P/D proxies' routing need. Splitting a replica across machines already comes from explicit replica placement.

## Decision

Add an optional per-role `devices` declaration. When it is declared, it is the sole authority for the role's whole-replica device count: integrations fill omitted components consistently with it, reject a declared shape that implies a different count under their own reading, and the control plane rejects a plan whose returned count differs. When it is absent, today's derivation is unchanged.

The existing parallelism components stay, but no longer as a framework-neutral vocabulary: they become a mapping onto framework options whose reading each integration owns and documents, and are deprecated in favor of `devices` plus framework-owned layout settings. Removing them is deferred to a later decision, after typed integration settings cover the layouts operators actually use and the data-parallel rank count has another source (the cache-owning target set). Until then `attention.data_parallel_size` remains the control plane's only source for the data-parallel rank count, so attention data parallelism stays declared through it rather than through framework settings or arguments.

This adds a protocol member and a record field and changes no existing declaration's meaning.

## Consequences

Positive: an operator can state the device count once and get the same placement under every integration; a layout that disagrees with it fails before launch instead of silently placing a different count. No existing workspace changes meaning, and vLLM keeps its native reading. Framework-specific layouts no longer need a neutral equivalent before they can be used together with `devices`.

Negative: until removal, two ways to express device count coexist, and declarations without `devices` keep the cross-integration ambiguity. Consistency checks cover only layout settings an integration renders; layout passed through framework arguments is judged by the framework at launch. Attention data parallelism expressed only through framework arguments would leave priming fan-out and built-in P/D proxy routing at one rank without failing; operator guidance keeps it in the vocabulary until the cache-owning target set provides the count. The adapter protocol version and the server record schema change.

## Alternatives Considered

### Canonicalize the vocabulary so outer is the replica world for every integration (rejected)

- **Pros:** One declaration means one device count and decomposition everywhere; records compare across frameworks
- **Cons:** Breaks vLLM's reading of existing declarations; keeps InferLab owning a vocabulary that must track ever finer per-component layouts, and context-parallel mechanisms already resist one rank identity

### Remove the parallelism vocabulary now; operators declare devices and layouts are framework settings (rejected)

- **Pros:** One placement authority with no neutral algebra left to maintain
- **Cons:** Breaks every workspace, the adapter protocol response, and records at once, before typed integration settings and the cache-owning target set exist to replace what the vocabulary still carries

### Derive the device count only in each integration from framework-native layout settings (rejected)

- **Pros:** No second declaration that can disagree with the layout
- **Cons:** Every integration keeps world algebra, and layouts passed through framework arguments or defined by a Specialized Engine cannot be derived at all

### Add an operator-declared devices count that wins when present and keep the vocabulary as deprecated option mapping (accepted)

- **Pros:** Placement becomes framework-independent without breaking any declaration; leaves time to design the vocabulary's removal
- **Cons:** Two ways to express device count coexist until removal; consistency is checked only for layout settings an integration renders
